The patient's history of asthma and the absence of low back pain also support this diagnosis. The diagnostic differences between peroneal nerve palsy and other candidate diseases, such as lumbar disc herniation and Guillain-Barre syndrome, include the location of pain, nerve conduction studies, and the pattern of muscle weakness.

The diagnostic differences between lumbar disc herniation and peroneal nerve palsy, such as the location of pain and nerve conduction studies, support peroneal nerve palsy as the more likely diagnosis.
